Answer: B
Reason: The serial chest X-rays (Figures 1a, 3a, 4a, 6a) demonstrate a clear progression from initial nodular densities in the middle and lower lung fields to extensive, diffuse bilateral infiltrative disease with areas of radiolucency (likely representing cavitation or emphysematous changes), consistent with advanced bronchioloalveolar carcinoma. Options suggesting stability, regression, or isolated upper lobe involvement are contradicted by the visual evidence of worsening diffuse pathology over time.
